What it is

Four ways into the same logbook.

Why I made it

One place for every flight and every trip

I’ve been an avgeek for as long as I can remember, and for almost two decades I’ve logged every flight on FlightMemory. It still holds my history, but it has aged badly. The newer contenders (OpenFlights, myFlightradar24, LogMy.World and others) each add a few features, but they also add complexity: unreliable imports, dull interfaces, and in the end, little value beyond yet another copy of the same data.

Then there’s my travel bug. Itineraries pinned in Google Maps. Visited cities logged in TripAdvisor. Countries ticked off in yet another app. And a separate list of every UNESCO World Heritage site I’d seen, kept up to date by hand.

And sharing a trip on Instagram? Tools like TravelBoast or Mult.dev feel childish, make you sit through ads, and charge a small fortune for a 20-second story that vanishes after 24 hours.

So after every trip, I had to update half a dozen platforms, and each one only showed a fragment of the journey.

Eventually I decided to fix it myself. I started a side project to automate the whole thing, and it grew into a single platform that does everything my way: my ideas, my data, my design.

That platform is my Boarding Past.
